projects.title: Planetary gear reducer
projects.description: I had planned to use the planetary gearbox for more powerful manipulator models. For now, a base unit has been created that transforms a standard electric motor into a functional robot joint.

projects.title: Omnidirectional wheels
projects.description: The experiment to create omnidirectional wheels was a success. I was simply testing my skills to see if I could model, 3D print, and assemble an omnidirectional wheel.

projects.title: Manipulator
projects.description: This robotic arm is built using very small N20 motors and an Arduino Nano controller. It receives commands via Bluetooth and can move objects between pre-programmed positions. It also features a color sensor for sorting items. The robot's gripper has been upgraded with sensor-equipped fingers to monitor gripping force and silicone pads to reduce slippage.

projects.title: all_terrain_vehicle
projects.description: The all-terrain robot is equipped with an ESP32-based camera and features a specialized tread design for navigating significant obstacles. Initial tests revealed some weaknesses, yet the robot already demonstrates good off-road capability.

projects.title: Bender's head
projects.description: Bender's head was created for a school holiday event. Children entered binary code on a control panel—black button for zero, green for one—and the robot would output a corresponding letter. Ultimately, the teams had to use these letters to assemble robot-themed versions of sayings and proverbs.

projects.title: Wilson the bug
projects.description: The robot is controlled via Bluetooth and has only two motors, with all the legs moving thanks to a parasitic gear drive. The robot model itself is currently lost.

projects.title: My Lego Instructions
projects.description: While working at a children's robotics school, I frequently had to update curricula and modernize my teaching approach; consequently, I developed numerous models for LEGO sets. Here are some of them. All of them utilize motors and at least one sensor.

projects.title: Simple robot hand for students
projects.description: A simple robotic manipulator for students. The design allows servomotors to rotate up to 180 degrees, protecting the motors from breaking and ensuring a safe programming experience for students.

projects.title: Quadropod
projects.description: A quadruped robot powered by servomotors. Model removed.

projects.title: Brooder for small birds
projects.description: Back when I was volunteering to rescue birds, I frequently took in chicks that couldn't survive without extra heat. So, I created these portable Arduino devices to control the precise temperature inside, making sure the nestlings stayed safe from both overheating and freezing.
